candidates.similarity: Divine favor and rainfall are connected with human obedience to God.
candidates.difference: Deuteronomy is a covenantal address to Israel regarding the land and warns of rain being withheld for other-god worship; Qur'an 11:52 addresses Ad through Hud and promises abundant rain upon repentance.
candidates.dating_note: Hebrew Bible text predates Islam as a tradition; the particular literary composition/redaction and extant manuscript witnesses must be documented separately before publication.

research_dossier.title: Hud and Ad: prophetic disinterest, repentance and rain
research_dossier.scope: Contrast Quranic Hud/Ad narrative with securely dated earlier prophetic and covenantal rain traditions; avoid unsupported equation of Ad with a Biblical people.
research_dossier.chronology_note: Dates of literary composition, editorial strata, and surviving witnesses for Hebrew texts must be separately reported; no verified external pre-Islamic identification of Hud or Ad is asserted.
research_dossier.comparison_note: 11:51 rejects monetary reward; 11:52 offers rain with repentance; 11:53-55 gives the response of Ad and Hud's challenge. The rain motif alone is not evidence of direct borrowing.
